messages.content: 紐約和華盛頓特區之間的行駛距離是多少？洛杉磯和舊金山之間的行駛距離是多少？請啟用最短路線的可選參數。

function.name: calc_distance
function.description: Calculate the driving distance between two locations. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

shortest_route.description: If true, returns the shortest driving route.

The user asks: "紐約和華盛頓特區之間的行駛距離是多少？洛杉磯和舊金山之間的行駛距離是多少？請啟用最短路線的可選參數。" They want distances between New York and Washington DC, and Los Angeles and San Francisco, using the optional parameter for shortest route.

We need to call the function twice: one for NY to DC, another for LA to SF. The function signature: start_loc: string, end_loc: string, shortest_route?: boolean (default false). We should set shortest_route=true.

Thus we will produce two function calls. According to guidelines, we can only output one function call at a time? Actually we can output multiple calls? The guidelines say: "When you do want to use a tool, you must do so by calling it with the name of the function and arguments." It doesn't explicitly forbid multiple calls. But typical pattern: we can call once, get result, then call again. But we might combine into one? The function expects single pair. So we need two separate calls. We can either call them sequentially or combine? Usually we call one, wait for response, then call next. But we can also ask for both? The function signature only accepts one pair. So we need two calls.

Thus we will first call calc_distance with start_loc="New York", end_loc="Washington DC", shortest_route=true. Then after receiving result, call again with start_loc="Los Angeles", end_loc="San Francisco", shortest_route=true.

But the instruction says "Please enable the optional parameter for shortest route." So we set shortest_route:true.

Thus we produce:

{
"name":"calc_distance",

}
}

Then after response, we call again.

But the user asked for both distances. We could respond with both results. But we can't compute without calling the function. So we need to call twice. We'll do first call.
